With enable_nccl_comm_suspend=True on NCCL 2.29.7 or newer, in-flight collectives are drained before ncclCommSuspend is invoked.
With expandable_segments enabled, the allocator automatically shrinks an expanded segment by unmapping its unused tail when memory pressure rises.
After a full level-1 sleep, calling release_kv_cache_memory() is accepted as a way to additionally drop the KV cache.
Slurm's gres/gpuutil for a step is sampled once at step end rather than during the run.
For our proposed NFD deployment, NFD can be used both to advertise detected node features as node labels and to taint those nodes so that only pods requesting those features are scheduled on them.

For the long-document workload, APC evicts the cached document's KV blocks in least-recently-used order once cache memory is exhausted.
In our proposed multi-GPU process, the allocator backend can be set to cudaMallocAsync for one device while the remaining devices keep the native backend.
A `--prefix-match-unit` value that does not divide a prefix-cacheable group's block size is silently rounded by vLLM to the nearest valid divisor.
Under the GPU GRES plugin, the salloc command exports a global CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES covering all GPUs in the allocation.

For our proposed node using AutoDetect=nvml with cgroup device constraint enabled, the CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES value seen by the Prolog may differ from the value seen by the job, and the slurmstepd's holding of the GPU library for per-step GPU accounting can be disabled with JobAcctGatherParams=DisableGPUAcct.

For the hybrid Mamba shared-prefix checkpoint under `--mamba-cache-mode align`, leaving `--prefix-match-unit` unset makes `--enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint` have no effect, and any value chosen must divide the block size of every prefix-cacheable KV cache group, which vLLM validates at startup.
Extended resources that NFD adds for GPUs can be consumed by a container through its resource limits in the same way as the device-plugin GPU resource.

In a release-only-KV flow with the pause completed and all executor memory resident, the documented CUDA configuration uses the default cumem backend with managed allocations, and release_kv_cache_memory discards KV cache physical memory while keeping model weights resident.
Node labels are the only output NFD can produce; it has no mechanism to add node taints.

For our proposed configuration, the cudaMallocAsync allocator backend selected through PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF requires CUDA 11.4 or newer, and the PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF name is accepted only as a backward-compatibility alias of that variable.
NFD re-detects hardware and updates a node's feature labels when a GPU is hot-added after the node has joined the cluster.
With sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph=True, graph executables that live outside PyTorch memory pools are removed from GPU memory during sleep rather than staying resident.
If a task's explicitly specified resources are unavailable at execution time, Ray preempts a running lower-priority task to free them.
With throw_on_cudamalloc_oom set to True, an allocation that would exceed the per_process_memory_fraction limit is rejected with an OutOfMemoryError before the driver allocation is attempted.
The documented Mamba checkpoint matching-unit recommendation requires the chosen value to be a multiple of the per-state compression ratio for a model that uses one.
With AccountingStorageTRES=gres/gpu and AutoDetect=nvml, Slurm also gathers gres/gpuutil for MIG devices.
Object store memory is a logical resource, so a task can request it to control where it is scheduled.
For our proposed actor that sets no explicit num_cpus, Ray by default will not schedule it on a zero-CPU node and will set OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 in its environment.
Calling empty_cache while tensors are still live releases the GPU memory occupied by those tensors for another process.
For our proposed container, after the vendor driver and device plugin are installed, a GPU limit can be specified without an explicit GPU request; Kubernetes uses that limit as the request.
For our proposed typed-GPU allocation, the job step should request GPUs of that same type.
For a request that shares an existing prefix, the documented APC benefit targets prompt processing rather than generation of new tokens.
The described GPU device plugin allows a container to request half of a physical GPU through its custom resource field.
A submission using the --gpus option will be accepted even when select/cons_tres is not configured.
APC keeps its cached prefix blocks available after a full server process restart.
Our proposed Ray task declaring num_cpus=1 is prevented by Ray from launching threads that use multiple physical CPUs.
Enabling APC lets a request with no prefix in common with existing queries reuse their prefix computations.
Starting a head node with zero logical CPUs can prevent CPU-requiring work from being scheduled there even when the machine has physical CPUs.
Disabling CUDA memory caching makes our training job finish faster than leaving caching enabled.
After waking only the model weights with tags=["weights"], is_sleeping can remain true until the remaining components are awake.
For the hybrid Mamba option described here, enabling the shared-prefix checkpoint flag is sufficient even when the model uses multi-module MTP.
The level-1 CPU backup of model weights is compressed before being stored in host memory.
For a cluster with different GPU types, node labels and selectors can steer a Pod to suitable nodes, and the label key does not have to be accelerator.
For the custom GPU resource described here, setting the request to one GPU and the limit to two GPUs is permitted.
The documented allocated-memory functions track tensors, whereas the reserved-memory functions track the total memory managed by the caching allocator.
Our current serving engine will finish waking from sleep in under five hundred milliseconds.
Our cluster has enough free GPUs of type tesla to start a two-GPU job right now.
Ray can move a running GPU actor to another node without restarting that actor.
The described PyTorch caching allocator uses first-fit selection to choose an available memory block.
Suspending a job makes its allocated generic resources available for other jobs to use.
In our proposed pause-and-resume workflow, level 1 sleep retains the existing KV-cache contents so requests resume with that unchanged cache.
Ray provides visible-device GPU isolation by setting CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, which most machine-learning frameworks respect for assignment.
